output.title: When rounding claims become a workflow decision
output.body:
If your business keeps hearing “rounding claims” as a vague complaint, the fix is to turn it into one bounded workflow decision. The real question is not whether numbers differ by a little; it is where those small gaps change what you do. That could be invoice rounding, currency conversion, timesheet variance, or an estimate-to-actual mismatch. Pick one recurring workflow and ask: which two slightly different numbers keep forcing someone to decide whether the gap matters?

Then draw the control boundary. Which cases are already policy, like rounding to the nearest cent? Which cases need human judgment, like flagging a gap above your own threshold? Which cases still have no rule at all? If the difference is invisible and acceptable, it can stay a background detail. If it is visible and affects approval or audit notes, it needs an explicit human step. Money movement stays human-approved.

The next practical step is simple: write one rounding rule in plain English for one recurring workflow. For example: “round amounts to the nearest cent; flag any gap above my threshold for review before I approve the invoice.” Then ask yourself one diagnostic question: do I already document why I accepted the difference, or do I just let it pass? If you cannot write the rule clearly yet, fix the policy first. The machine can wait; paperwork usually does not.
